bugs.title: analysis_720p.mp4 is generated and uploaded to every Stage A release but never read downstream — stop generating/uploading it
bugs.notes: VERIFIED CLAIM INDEPENDENTLY: grep across the repo (excluding .git/_legacy) confirmed analysis_720p.mp4 was referenced only in .github/workflows/stage-a.yml, pipeline/stage_a/bundle.py, pipeline/tests/test_stage_a.py, schemas/analysis_bundle.schema.json (one reference the prompt did not list — the asset-name/purpose enums, also fixed), and ARCHITECTURE.md (docs table row). Nothing in pipeline/plan/, pipeline/stage_b/, or bot/ ever read it. FIX: (1) stage-a.yml 'Probe duration + build 720p analysis copy' step renamed to 'Probe source duration' — the load-bearing ffprobe duration probe (DURATION_SECONDS) kept verbatim, the full 720p ffmpeg transcode removed entirely. (2) The two consumers of the 720p file in stage-a.yml — 'Local vision-assist stack' (scenes all) and 'Vision-assist disabled' grid generation — now read the original source directly via ORIGINAL_PATH (each step now resolves ORIGINAL_PATH from ingest.json itself; both steps already had the ingest.json read pattern in sibling steps); these steps run only on fresh ingests (not series reuse), so reading the full-quality original is correct and arguably higher quality than the 720p proxy. (3) series_reuse block: removed analysis_720p.mp4 from the gh release download pattern list, removed the hard post-condition check that exited 1 when it was missing (the bug-47-era requirement), and removed the copy into work/analysis/. (4) bundle.py: removed ('analysis_720p.mp4', 'analysis_copy_720p', False) from BUNDLE_ASSETS, removed the analysis_mp4 location/legacy-fallback/require block (work/analysis/compressed.mp4 fallback deleted too — it existed only for the 720p contract), removed it from the staged copy dict, updated module docstring. (5) schemas/analysis_bundle.schema.json: removed 'analysis_720p.mp4' from the name enum and 'analysis_copy_720p' from the purpose enum — validated with jsonschema that a new-shape manifest validates and a stale entry is now rejected. (6) ARCHITECTURE.md §7.2 table row removed. (7) Tests: _stage_work no longer fabricates analysis_720p.mp4; test_run_bundle_produces_contract_assets updated to the new asset set plus negative assertions (asset not in manifest names, file not in bundle dir, purpose enum absent). TESTS RUN: full pipeline suite 305 passed + 52 subtests, 10 failed — the exact same 10 pre-existing unrelated failures as unmodified main (test_stage_a telegram-relay x2 = sandbox disk-space preflight, test_stage_b ReframeDetectionTier x7, test_status x1), confirmed identical via git stash A/B. Workflow YAML parses. Zero new failures.

bugs.title: Stage A releases fail outright when source_input.bin exceeds GitHub's 2 GiB per-asset limit — retry release without source, Stage B re-fetches source from stage-a-request.json
bugs.notes: DONE. Implementation landed across two prior-session commits (d45064d refetch_source module + 11 tests; 0a6c0a6 stage-a retry gate + stage-b re-fetch + ARCHITECTURE.md) plus three this-session commits (f1edda8 upload-corruption fix, 6376810 gate extraction + 8 tests, 6ea19ec 9 workflow-shape tests). THIS SESSION'S VERIFICATION + FIXES: (1) FOUND+FIXED a real corruption bug in the prior session's retry path: the retry's asset re-uploads and the manifest re-upload used 'gh api -F data=@file', which I proved empirically (local HTTP request-capture stub, gh v2.98.0) JSON-ENCODES the bytes ({"data":"\\u0000..."}, 4223B for a 1024B file — stored asset is corrupted JSON, not the file). Since the retry path is the primary path for this feature, every omitted-source release would have shipped unreadable transcript/scene/key-moments/screenshots/manifest assets. Fixed both call sites to 'gh api --input <file>' (proved byte-identical, 1024/1024) — commit f1edda8. (2) Extracted the untested inline 2 GiB classification heredoc into pipeline/stage_a/release_gate.py (identical logic) and pinned all four failure shapes in pipeline/tests/test_release_gate.py (8 tests): oversized+prefix->retry, oversized+missing prefix->refail, within-limit->refail, release-never-created->refail, event_composites prefix handling, CLI exit codes — commit 6376810. The workflow now runs the tested module, not a drifting copy. (3) Added pipeline/tests/test_bug69_release_retry_shape.py (9 parsed-YAML structural tests) pinning the full-bundle continue-on-error primary attempt, --input raw-byte uploads, delete-before-rePOST idempotency, source-omitted body/manifest markers, Stage B source_found gating, and mutually-exclusive download/refetch steps — commit 6ea19ec. VERIFY CHECKLIST (prompt): stage-a-request.json confirmed to durably persist source.kind/value/relay{release_tag,expected_size_bytes,sha256}/torrent_file_index for every kind via bot's buildStageARequest + wizardToRequest, and pickTorrentFile re-saves torrent_file_index after the interactive selection (bot/src/index.js) — NO missing-field gap for any kind (incl. telegram_relay, whose relay block refetch reuses directly). Normal path zero-change (download step gated on source_found=true). Failure+retry path: classification tested; retry idempotency (delete-leftover-then-POST) and omission recording (body source-omitted:true + manifest source_omitted/source_omitted_reason, source_input.bin entry dropped) pinned by shape tests. Stage B re-fetch tested for torrent (exact saved torrent_file_index, interactive parking never re-triggered) and direct URL. Series interaction: series_reuse downloads evidence separately, tries Part 1 release source first, falls through to refetch_source --source-job <part1> (Part 1's original source.torrent manifest honoured as-is). All 12 embedded python heredocs across both workflows compile. TESTS: pipeline suite 333 passed + 52 subtests, 10 failed — the EXACT same 10 pre-existing unrelated failures as unmodified main (telegram-relay x2 sandbox disk preflight, ReframeDetectionTier x7 OpenCV/cascade env, test_status x1), zero new failures; bot suite 140/140 pass. NOTE: real-world end-to-end validation of the >2 GiB path requires an actual oversized source on a live runner (cannot be simulated in the offline sandbox); every offline-testable component is covered.
